name: Volvariella volvacea

size_cm.note: cap 5 to 12 cm across; stem 6 to 12 cm long

notes: Very fast, and grows from an egg-like sac. Reported (unchecked) to have the fastest crop cycle of the cultivated mushrooms, to be killed by chilling and to have a sequenced genome.

tip_speed.note: colony radius growth 0.0503 +/- 0.001 cm/h for the undegenerated commercial strain V971 on PDA (Chen, Zhang, Liu, Cui, Miao, Cheng & Zhao 2019, Characteristics analysis reveals the progress of Volvariella volvacea mycelium subculture degeneration, Frontiers in Microbiology 10:2045, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6733957/); x 10,000 = 503 um/h. Strains in that paper were kept at 30 C, below the 35 C optimum, and the rate was not corrected, so this is likely a little low. Degenerated subcultures fell to 0.041 cm/h

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.source: Kiran Kumar, Krishnamoorthy, Kamalakannan & Amirtham 2016, Influence of temperature and pH on mycelial growth and chlamydospore production of paddy straw mushroom Volvariella volvaceae (Bull. ex Fr.) Sing., The Journal of Research ANGRAU 44(1&2):1-7
t_opt.note: strain CBE TNAU 1505, tested 15 to 40 C; most mycelial growth at about 35 C. Chang & Steinkraus 1982 give 37 C (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC241845/)

t_min.note: growth was poor below 20 C in a 15 to 40 C series (Kiran Kumar et al. 2016, https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/TJRA/article/view/140244), and below 15 C the mycelium is damaged and loses viability (Bao et al. 2013, PLoS ONE 8(3):e58294, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3602538/); 15 C taken as the limit. Chang & Steinkraus 1982 give a minimum of 25 C

t_max.source: Chang & Steinkraus 1982, Lignocellulolytic enzymes produced by Volvariella volvacea, the edible straw mushroom, Applied and Environmental Microbiology 43(2):440-446
t_max.note: abstract: minimum 25 C, optimum 37 C, maximum 40 C; medium and strain not given in the abstract. Kiran Kumar et al. 2016 also found growth poor above 40 C

cold_drop.note: growth and fruiting share one warm range, 28 to 35 C, and chilling below 15 C does damage (Bao et al. 2013, PLoS ONE 8(3):e58294, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3602538/), so no temperature drop is needed
